title: Towards Neurosymbolic AI for Risk Assessment in Geological Hazards
description:
The project investigates how artificial intelligence can support reasoning under incomplete and uncertain information in volcanic monitoring, taking bradyseism at Campi Flegrei (Naples) as its main case study. It is organized along three complementary lines of research.

Data science. Carried out in collaboration with Prof. Angelo Ciaramella (DIST, University of Naples Parthenope) and INGV – Osservatorio Vesuviano, this line provides an in-depth characterization of the GNSS deformation signal: its structure, its temporal behaviour and its components, from the bradyseismic trend to the irreducible noise. Building on this analysis, it defines an end-to-end processing pipeline that compares the available positioning solutions to assess their reliability, separates the deformation signal from spurious components, and characterizes the residual noise. The resulting time series are employed for ground deformation forecasting, with particular emphasis on uncertainty quantification and model interpretability. A central objective is to assess whether hourly solutions, which are considerably noisier, can attain a quality at least comparable to that of daily solutions, thereby enabling more frequent assessments than those currently provided by the weekly bulletins.

Logic. This line introduces intuitionistic temporal and strategic logics (ICTL, IATL), which capture the progressive refinement of knowledge, together with their model checking within VITAMIN. These formalisms allow the monitoring system itself to be modelled as a multi-agent system, describing how stations, reference stations and processing components behave under varying environmental conditions (signal degradation, missing references, seismic swarms), and enabling the formal verification of its properties.

Generative models. This line addresses the automatic translation of natural-language scenario descriptions into verifiable formal models, allowing scenarios expressed in natural language to be formally verified.

Data analysis and formal reasoning thus provide two complementary perspectives: the former extracts reliable information on ground deformation, while the latter verifies the behaviour of the monitoring system. Together, they define a neurosymbolic framework for volcanic monitoring, which is further extended to cascading hazards such as landslides.
tech: GNSS Signal Analysis, Time Series Forecasting, Uncertainty Quantification, Explainable AI, Temporal and Strategic Reasoning, Model Checking, Generative Models, Neurosymbolic AI.

title: APLAND – AI for Landslide Susceptibility Mapping
description: APLAND is an applied research initiative focused on developing AI-driven tools for landslide susceptibility assessment. In collaboration with BIDATA, I contributed to the modelling pipeline by designing and implementing a data-driven workflow based on the Frequency Ratio (FR) method for generating susceptibility maps. The project integrates geospatial data, environmental conditioning factors, and machine-learning components to support risk analysis and decision-making for territorial monitoring and civil protection.
tech: AI Modeling, Explainable AI, Geospatial Data Analysis, Frequency Ratio Method, Multimodal Data Integration, Neuro-Symbolic Methods, FastAPI, Geoserver, Rasterio, Streamlit.

title: VITAMIN – Model Checker
description: Working with the ASTREA research team, I am involved in the engineering and development of VITAMIN, a model checker designed for verifying complex systems. My focus is on optimizing the processing of input data, refactoring and testing the code, and enhancing readability. I have also implemented model checking for two new formalisms: Intuitionistic CTL and Intuitionistic ATL. As part of my research visit at Télécom Paris, I am developing generative models for the automatic construction of formal models from natural-language scenario descriptions, which will be integrated into VITAMIN. Future developments include the extension of the tool to further logics, namely a generalization of ICTL and IATL and a fuzzy variant of IATL.

title: Food Talk
description: As part of the Agritech Academy, I collaborated with a team to develop an application designed to optimize the traceability of fresh produce from production to consumption. The system streamlines the supply chain, offering real-time insights to improve quality control and enhance market transparency.
tech: Mobile and Web Development, Data Integration, Process Optimization.

title: Wine – Digital Sommelier Assistant
description: Wine is a mobile application designed for sommeliers to digitally compile tasting sheets for the Italian Association of Sommeliers. The collected data is then used by a recommendation system to suggest the ideal wine for various occasions.
tech: Mobile App Development, Data-Driven Recommendation Systems.

title: Medical Survey
description: Medical Survey is a web polling application that enables conference attendees to respond to questions in real time, with immediate display of results. Currently deployed in scientific medical conferences, this tool significantly enhances audience engagement and feedback collection.
tech: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Firebase, Cloud Computing.

title: Theatrical Digital Archive – Certosa di San Martino, Naples
description: During my Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, I developed an application tailored to the conservation and exhibition needs of the "Fondo Niccolini" – a collection of over 900 artworks. By digitizing and systematically archiving these works, museum visitors can explore the collection through thematic classification and a tree-structured exploration of various topics.
tech: Java, Usability Testing, REST APIs, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Neo4J, Cypher Query Language.
